result:
Confirmed — there's no separate immediate-email job; `email` is a delivery channel that only ever leaves the building through the digest job. Now the full path.

## The whole path

**What starts the check.** `startScheduler()` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` (invoked from `src/instrumentation.ts` at boot) runs `setInterval(tick, 60_000)`. Every tick, `tick(now)` walks the `CADENCE_MINUTES` table and, once an hour (`"overdue-issues": 60`), calls `isDue("overdue-issues", now)`, `enqueue(...)`, and `drain()`, which runs `runOverdueIssueJob` from the queue. The same job is independently reachable via `POST /api/cron/overdue` (`src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`), which checks `assertCronSecret` and calls `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())` directly — an external cron trigger for the same code path, not a second implementation.

**Narrowing the set of issues that count.** `runOverdueIssueJob` (`src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`) first sanity-checks `shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_ONLY)` (from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`) and bails with a warning if archive scoping is misconfigured, so a config bug can't leak archived issues into the sweep. It then pages through orgs via `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(ORG_BATCH)` and, per org, calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts:507`). That query is the actual filter: issue belongs to the org, is not archived (`livePredicate`), has a non-null `dueAt` in the past (`lt(issues.dueAt, now)`), and its status is one of `backlog | todo | in_progress | in_review` — done/cancelled issues never qualify.

**What the job does and doesn't own.** For each returned issue, if it's already in the in-memory `reported` Set the job skips it silently; otherwise it calls `emit("issue.overdue", { orgId, actorId: null, occurredAt, issueId, projectId, dueAt, assigneeId })` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`) and only then adds the id to `reported`. The job's responsibility ends at announcing the fact on the event bus — it does not decide who gets told, through which channel, or with what wording; that's explicitly left to subscribers (per its own header comment).

**What stops repeat announcements.** The `reported` Set in `overdue-issue-job.ts` is the sole guard: once an issue id is added, the next hourly sweep (and any cron-triggered sweep) finds it still overdue but skips it because `reported.has(issue.id)` is true, so `emit` is never called again for that issue in this process's lifetime. (`resetOverdueTracking()` exists only for tests to clear this state between scenarios.) This means the "no repeats" guarantee lives at the emission layer, not at the notification layer — the fan-out below has no dedupe logic of its own for this event.

**How the alert reaches one specific person.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` calls `registerFanOut()` at module load, which subscribes to `"issue.overdue"`. The handler bails out if `payload.assigneeId === null` (no assignee, no alert), otherwise calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [payload.assigneeId], { title, body, href, actorId: null })`. `notify()` looks up the org for flag context, then for each recipient (here, just the one assignee) calls `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "issue_overdue")` and runs it through `resolveChannels(preference, flags)`: no stored preference defaults to `["in_app", "email"]`; a stored preference includes `in_app` only if `preference.inApp`, and includes `email` only if `preference.email` is true and either `digestOnly` is false or the org's `digest_email` flag is on. If the resolved channel list is empty, the recipient is skipped entirely — no row, no alert. Otherwise `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` writes one row carrying that channel set, which is what the recipient actually sees: the `in_app` channel surfaces through `listNotifications`/the notification UI, while the `email` channel is realized later by `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`), which — once per org per day, during that org's configured `digestHourUtc` — bundles the recipient's unread notifications via `buildDigest`/`digest-service.ts` and calls `sendEmail` (`src/server/services/email-service.ts`, which logs the "send" since this app has no real mail transport). So the channels the person "chose" are their stored `NotificationPreference` row, edited through `notification-preferences-form.tsx` and `updatePreference` in the same service, and they determine both whether the alert shows up in-app and whether/how it eventually reaches them by email.
